newsitem.title: FINLAND: LIPPONEN CALLS FOR LOW-INFLATION PAY DEAL FROM '98.
newsitem.headline: LIPPONEN CALLS FOR LOW-INFLATION PAY DEAL FROM '98.

text.p: Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen on Thursday called on the labour market organisations to look at the positive results of the current incomes settlement and try to reach similar low-inflationary pay deals from 1998 onwards.
He said the government would not meddle in the collective bargaining talks, but the size of future income tax cuts would depend partly on the level of pay rises agreed between unions and employers.
"It is a central goal for the government to promote moderate labour market agreements that secure low inflation," Lipponen told a briefing for journalists.
"The government will not push for any incomes settlement model," he said, adding the size, shape and duration of the pay deals must be decided by the labour market organisations themselves.
"The government thinks that the experiences of the current agreements will encourage (unions and employers) to continue with the (incomes settlement) policy of low inflation," he said.

Lipponen praised the current nation-wide low-pay-rise agreement reached in the autumn of 1995 and running until February 1998. It had provided the foundation for Finnish competitiveness and low inflation, he said.
"The taxation of wage earners has been eased and purchasing power has developed better than forecast," he said.
Any new income tax cuts would be "dimensioned according to the possibilities of the state finances and taking the incomes settlements into consideration," Lipponen said.
